frames.reasons: Looked at the backlit wall face, the shadowed floor strip in front of it, the sunlit floor wedges at the left and right edges, and the sky. Both BEFORE runs match each other, and so do both AFTER runs. In AFTER the wall face is a little darker and less warm, and the shadowed floor is slightly darker. Both moves are toward Unreal's much darker wall and near-black floor. The lit side wedges and the wall's top edge did not change. No banding, clipping or leaks.
frames.differences: Unreal's backlit wall is much darker and a neutral charcoal (AFTER is still warm brown and clearly brighter). Unreal's shadowed floor is near black. The cloud shapes and colours differ, and Unreal shows a dark band of distant terrain at the horizon behind the wall's ends.

frames.reasons: Looked at the capsule body, the white spheres, the red and white cubes, the lit floor on the left, the shadow wedge on the right, and the emissive sphere's glow on the floor. AFTER is only slightly dimmer on the lit floor and capsule, close to Unreal's level. Shadow edges, the glow and the red cube are unchanged. No new artefacts.
frames.differences: Unreal's metal sphere is a matte grey diffuse ball, while ThreeNative's is a mirror-chrome sky reflection (present in both arms). Unreal shows a faint green tint on the white cube's shaded side. The clouds differ.

frames.reasons: Looked at the back wall, the left and right side walls, the ceiling, the floor and the corner seams. AFTER darkens the whole room. The back wall moves toward Unreal's level. But the ceiling (charcoal in AFTER, where Unreal's is a lighter blue-grey that BEFORE's was close to), the side walls (now clearly darker than Unreal's) and the floor (near black in AFTER, where Unreal's is a visibly lighter navy) all move away from Unreal. AFTER also shows a faint, slightly bluish lighter patch at the lower centre of the back wall in both runs. It is weak and Unreal has a similar faint lift there, so I do not count it as an artefact. The darker ceiling, side walls and floor are the regression.
frames.differences: Unreal's room has a cool blue-grey sky-fill tint on every surface, where ThreeNative's is neutral grey. The ceiling, side walls and floor in AFTER are darker than Unreal's. The back wall level is now close.

overall.reasons: The backlit frames on L7 and L8 improve: the wall and shadowed floor move toward Unreal's darker values. The sphere frames and most L9 frames are neutral. Three frames regress visibly. In both sun60 interiors (L7 and L8), the overall darkening fixes the back wall but pushes the ceiling, side walls and floor clearly darker than Unreal, where BEFORE was close to them in level. In L9 sun04 exterior, the large sunlit floor loses orange saturation and shifts away from Unreal's orange. The criteria fail a round on one REGRESSION in any frame, so this round fails. Against Unreal, AFTER has the same lighting structure everywhere, with named differences: a cool sky tint missing indoors, a backlit wall that is too warm and bright at sun04, and floor warmth.
